section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1981
title: 28 Means adopted to Commit Suicides : A study of Suicide cases according to the 'Means Adopted' for committing Suicides revealed that the majority of persons committed suicide by 'Hanging' during 1981 and 23·7 per cent of the total suicides were committed by this method. The other second important mean used for committing suicides was by taking poison and 22·1 per cent of the total suicides were committed by this method during 1981 followed by 'Drowning' (17·3%), by 'Fire' (8·9%), by 'Railways' (6·5%), by 'Fire-arms' (1·3%), by 'Jumping' (1·3%), by 'Weapons' (1·0%), and by 'Machine' (0·4%), while 17·5 per cent of the total suicides registered during 1981 was shared by the suicides grouped under 'Other Causes'. The details are presented in Table-IV.
